newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK -Bradys cheap, Euros sidelined.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK -Bradys cheap, Euros sidelined.

text.p: An alleged cash-for-votes scandal has widened Brazilian Brady spreads to enticing levels, but the scam and jitters about a new U.S. rate increase will keep Eurobond players sidelined next week, market watchers said.

For the first time ever, the Brazilian sub index of J.P. Morgan's Emerging Market Bond Index traded at a wider spread than the index as a whole this week, according to Morgan's fixed-income analyst in Brazil Tina Vandersteel.

"Brazilian Brady's have cheapened relative to the index so, if no (scandal-related) news comes out over the weekend, then people may start to get optimistic, or at least not negative about Brazil," Vandersteel said.
Still, Brady traders were advising caution ahead of a week that promised to bring some volatility.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting is set for Tuesday, with analysts seeing a better than 50-50 chance of a 25 basis point increase in short-term rates.
Also Tuesday, Brazilian lawmakers are expected to take up the controversial re-election bill, which if delayed, could cause more worries in local markets

And on Wednesday, Brazilian economic policy-makers meet to set June interest rates, with local markets no longer certain about the government's interest rate policy after ending a steady policy of easing last month.
"I would advise staying on the sidelines at this point," said Pedro Barbosa, head of Brady trading at ING Bank in Brazil.

THE EUROBOND PRIMARY MARKET should see few Brazilian issues next week as a result of the uncertainty, traders said. There was talk in the market that Petrobras had selected Daiwa to do a 30 billion yen six-year samurai bond, but the issue wasn't expected before late June.

IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds ended the week mostly flat, escaping the sharp dives in the Brady market that were triggered by the alleged money-for-votes scandal involving a key cabinet official.
The sharpest Eurobond gains were seen in high-yield bonds like Tevecap's 12.625 percent due 2004 ZRIT, which tightened 17 basis points to 504 bp over Treasuries.

Other top performing high-yield bonds included TV Filme's 12.875 percent due 2004 (call 03), which narrowed seven basis points to 535. Both bonds continued to be supported by steady flows into high yield funds, debt watchers said.

"TV Filme has performed quite well, tightening 56 basis points over the last month. But the best performer has been Tevecap, which has narrowed 71 basis points in that time," said Matthew Peck, a corporate bond analyst for Salomon Brothers.

ATTTRACTIVE BUYS include Eletrobras 10 percent due 2004 (put 01) ZSED, which widened five bp to 223 bp over during the week. The Eletrobras bond is one of Brazil's most liquid Eurobonds and suffered more than other corporate issues by the selloff in the Brady market, market players said.

Eletrobras took down other energy bonds, such as Cesp's 9.25 percent due 2001 ZSED and Furnas' 9.0 percent due 2005 ZXLW. Traders expected the three bonds to outperform other corporates next week barring any negative local news.
